 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVAN M. DESAI  Date : 07/08/2025
ORAL ORDER 1.

The present First Appeal is filed under Section 30 of The Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 by appellant - original respondent No.2 challenging the judgment and award dated 30.03.2024 passed by the learned Workman Compensation Commissioner, Labour Court No.1, Jamnagar in Workman Compensation (Non-Fatal) Case No.14 of 2016, whereby the application of claimant/s was partly allowed.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 2.

Heard learned advocate Mr.K.V.Gadhia for the appellant - original respondent No.2 and learned The New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Guardian Of Ubez Sagirkhan Pathan, ... on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191625791/

sentences.text: advocate Mr.Yogen Pandya for respondent No.1 - original claimant.
Though served, none appeared for respondent No.2.
By order dated 11.02.2005, Co- ordinate Bench of this Court has issued notice for final disposal of present Appeal.

3. Brief facts narrated in the present First Appeal are as under:-
3.1
The son of original applicant was employed in the employment of original opponent No.1.
On 04.06.2016, while operating a machine during the course of his employment, workman sustained serious injuries as his hand was trapped in the machine.
As a result, the tip of third finger on his right hand was NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined severed.
The age of the employee was 12 years at the relevant point of time.
3.2 The injured was taken to the hospital.

As the employer did not pay compensation within the stipulated time as prescribed under the Act, the father being a natural guardian of injured, filed a claim petition against the employer and Insurance Company.
3.3 The claim petition was contested by opponent No.1 by filing Written Statement at Ex.11.
The Insurance Company - original opponent No.2 also contested the claim petition by filing Written Statement at Ex.33.
Applicant examined himself at Ex.34 and produced documentary evidences.
Original opponent No.1 also examined himself at Ex.60 and produced documentary evidence.

After considering the evidence on record, learned Commissioner partly allowed the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined petition and directed both opponents to pay compensation of Rs.67,383/- along with interest at the rate of 12% per annum and 50% penalty.
3.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award, Insurance Company - appellant has preferred the present appeal.

4. Learned advocate for the appellant contended that the challenge in the present appeal is based mainly on two grounds; firstly, the employee and employer relationship was never established by the appellant; and secondly, the learned Commissioner has erred in awarding interest against the Insurance Company which is contrary to settled position of law.
4.1

It is further contended that there is no evidence on record to establish the relationship of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined employee and employer and the learned Commissioner has committed a grave error by holding that the relationship has been established.

So far as allowing interest is concerned, it is submitted that the policy in question was a Workmen's Compensation Policy and as per terms and conditions of the policy, liability of interest as the liability of interest was excluded in the policy.

In support of his contention, learned advocate for the appellant has referred the decision of New India Assurance Co.
The New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Guardian Of Ubez Sagirkhan Pathan, ... on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191625791/
2 Ltd. Vs. Harshadbhai Amrutbhai Modhiya and Anr.

reported in 2006 AIR SCW 2352.
5.

Per contra, learned advocate for respondent No.1 has supported the judgment and award and contended that the claimant has established the relationship of employee and employer between the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined son of claimant and opponent No.1 by leading cogent and convincing evidence.
It is further submitted that the scope under Section 30 of the Workmen's Compensation Act is limited, and unless there are substantial questions of law involved, no appeal can be entertained.
It is further submitted that the question of relationship is not a question of law but it is a pure question of fact.
5.1 So far as the liability of interest is concerned, learned advocate for respondent could not contradict the settled proposition of law as held in the decision of Harshadbhai (supra).
6. I have considered the submissions canvassed by learned advocates for the respective parties and also perused the record and proceedings.
Son of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined claimant, who was aged about 12 years, was serving with present respondent No.2.
On 04.06.2016, while performing his duties at the premises of opponent No.1, he sustained injuries.
A claim petition was filed claiming compensation of Rs.1,49,789/-.
Learned Commissioner after considering the evidence on record granted compensation of Rs.67,383/- against the appellant herein as well as against the employer.

Considering non involvement of any substantial question of law as well as the smallness of amount involved in the present appeal, I do not find any reason to interfere in the finding of fact so far as compensation is concerned.

7. The only question which is required to be considered is whether fastening of interest liability on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined Insurance Company is justifiable or not.
The question of impositing liability of interest on Insurance Company is no more res-integra in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Harshadbhai Amrutbhai Modhiya and Anr.

8. In the case of Hiralal Gomaji Moriya (supra), the Co-ordinate Bench has observed in para Nos.10,
11, 12 and 13 which are reproduced hereinbelow:-
"10.

Thus, the law is settled on this aspect that the statutory liability under the Workmen's Compensation Act is on the employer and unless a separate clause NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined included for the liability of interest
, the Insurance Company.
is not liable to make payment of interest especially in case where the accident is not related to a motor vehicle accident.

sentences.text: Now corning to the question of penalty is concerned, the observation made by the Apex Court in the case of Ved Prakash Garg v. Premi Devi and others, reported in (1997) 8 SCC 1 is relevant.

entities.text: Ved Prakash Garg v. Premi Devi and others, reported in (1997) 8 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case the Apex Court after examining the entire scheme of the Act held that payment of interest and penalty are two distinct liabilities arising under the Act, while liability to pay interest is part and parcel of legal liability to pay compensation upon default of payment of that amount within one month.
Therefore, claim for compensation along with interest will have to be made good jointly by the Insurance company with the insured employer.
But, so far as the penalty imposed on the insured employer is on account of his personal fault, the insurance company cannot be made liable to reimburse penalty imposed on employer.
Hence the compensation with interest is payable by the insurance company but not penalty.
12. Thus, the Insurance Company is not liable to make the payment of penalty.

As regards the interest liability as held in the case of Ved Prakash (supra) is concerned,
the same was distinguished on facts.
In the said case it was a case where an accident has occurred by use of motor vehicle in respect whereof the contract of insurance would be governed by the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Therefore, the Insurance Company was held liable.

13. The above proposition has been laid down in the case of New India Assurance Co.
Ltd v. Harshadbhai Amrutbhai Modhiya and Another, reported in 2006 AIR SCW 2352.

Para 24 of the said decision reads as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined "24.Section 17 of the Workmen's Compensation Act voids only a contract or agreement whereby a workman relinquishes any right of compensation from the employer for personal injury arising out of or in the course of the employment and insofar as it purports to remove or reduce the liability of any person to pay compensation under the Act.
As my learned brother has noticed.

in the Workmen's Compensation Act, there are no provisions corresponding to those in the Motor Vehicles Act, insisting on the insurer covering the entire liability arising out of an award towards compensation to a third party arising out of a motor accident.

It is not brought to our notice that there is any other law enacted which stands in the way of an insurance company and the insured entering into a contract confining the obligation of the insurance company to indemnify to a particular head or to a particular amount when it relates to a claim for compensation to a third party arising under the Workmen's Compensation Act.
In this situation, the obligation of the insurance company clearly stands limited and a relevant proviso providing for exclusion of liability for interest or penalty has to be given effect to.

Unlike the scheme of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Workmen's Compensation Act, does not confer a right on the claimant for compensation under that Act to claim the payment of compensation in its entirety from the insurer himself.

The entitlement of the claimant under the Workmen's Compensation Act is to claim the compensation from The New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Guardian Of Ubez Sagirkhan Pathan, ... on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191625791/
4 the employer.

sentences.text: As between the employer and the insurer, the rights and obligations would depend upon the terms of the insurancecontract

Construing the contract involved here it is clear that the insurer has specifically excluded any liability for interest or penalty under NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED:
07/08/2025 undefined the Workmen's Compen-sation Act and confined its liability to indemnify the employer only against the amount of compensation ordered to be paid under the Workmen's Compen- sation Act.
The High Court was.
therefore, not correct in holding that the appellant- insurance company, is also liable to pay the interest on the amount of compensation awarded by the Commissioner.

The workman has to recover it from the employer."
9.
Considering the aforesaid established legal position, learned Commissioner has committed grave of error of law by awarding interest on the Insurance Company.
The award of interest against Insurance Company is against the settled position of law and therefore, a substantial question of law is involved in this Appeal.
In the present case, the policy being a Workman Compensation Policy, which exonerates Insurance Company from indemnifying insured against interest liability.
Insured and Insurer are governed by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined the Contract.

When a particular term of the contract excludes Insurance Company from indemnifying insured,
Insurance Company cannot be saddled with the liability of payment of interest.

10. In view of the aforesaid discussions and settled proposition of law, the judgment and award dated 30.03.2024 passed by the learned Workman Compensation Commissioner, Labour Court No.1, Jamnagar in Workman Compensation (Non-Fatal) Case No.14 of 2016, is hereby modified.
11. The Insurance Company is exonerated from the liability of payment of interest to the claimant/s.

The claimant/s shall be entitled to interest at the rate of 12% from the date of accident till realization from NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4218/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined the employer-original opponent No.1.
The learned Commissioner shall refund any excess amount to the Insurance Company - appellant after following due procedure.
Remaining amount shall be disbursed in favour of the claimant/s in accordance with due procedure.
12. In view of the above observations and directions, the present First Appeal is partly allowed.

Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Court/Tribunal forthwith.
13.
In view of the order passed in the main matter, connected Civil Application does not survive and stands disposed of accordingly.
